title: JKJAAC appeals for end to military operation in Rawalakot
seoTitle: Rawalakot JKJAAC appeals against military ops

tea.why: Protesters are demanding political, economic, and governance reforms.
tea.want: End military operations, withdraw security personnel, and initiate dialogue.
tea.changed: Nov 5: Pakistani security forces launched an operation in Rawalakot, resulting in reported deaths and injuries.

summary: The Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JKJAAC) has appealed directly to Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir to halt military operations in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. The appeal follows a security operation in Rawalakot to clear protest camps, which reportedly left at least seven people dead and around 23 injured. Organisers accused security forces of using heavy weapons and drones against demonstrators. The committee claims that over 150 people have died since the agitation began. Protesters are demanding political and governance reforms, accountability for deaths, and a return to dialogue, rejecting attempts by authorities to label the movement as terrorism. Pakistani police accused members of the movement of attacking law enforcement personnel.
organizers: Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JKJAAC)
demands: End to military operations in PoK
response: According to the sources, Pakistani security forces launched an operation to clear protest camps, using heavy weapons and drones. Pakistani police accused members of the protest movement of attacking law enforcement personnel.

deaths.text: more than 150 people have died in connection with the protests

updates.text: Security forces launched an operation in Rawalakot to clear protest camps, resulting in reported casualties.
The JKJAAC appealed to Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir to stop military operations and start negotiations.
